BILL NUMBER:  S3635

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to revising the
standards relating to the incorporation of stock or mutual insurance
companies


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To revise the standards relating to the incorporation of stock or
mutual insurance companies so that the incorporators of an insurance
corporation need only list their city and state of residence in
newspapers and the company charter. This bill would also reduce the
number of directors from thirteen to seven. The bill also removes the
requirement that not less than two directors be residents of New York
State. The bill would also reduce the number of officers who must be
directors from two to one.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
This bill would amend Section 1201(a)(3) of the Insurance Law to
remove the requirement that the proposed incorporators of a New York
insurance corporation publish in a newspaper their residence address
and require, instead, that they only publish their city and state of
residence. The bill would also amend Section 1201(a)(5)(vii) to remove
the requirement that the residence address of the proposed
incorporators be contained in the corporate charter and require.
instead, that they only publish their city and state of residence.

In addition, Sections 1201(a)(5)(v), 1202(a) (2), and 1209(b) of the
Insurance Law would be amended to reduce the number of directors
necessary to incorporate a stock or mutual insurance company from
thirteen to seven. Section 1201(a)(5)(vi) would be amended to remove
the requirement that not less than two directors be residents of New
York State. The bill would also amend Section 1209(c) to reduce the
number of officers who must be a director from two to one.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The requirement that the incorporators of a new insurance corporation
in New York must publicize their home addresses has been a potential
impediment to the formation of new companies in the state. It is
understandable that these individuals would be uncomfortable with
disclosing their home addresses in the newspaper and it is not
essential for the public to know this information.  Rather, it appears
that publication of the city and state of residence would be
sufficient for this purpose.

In today's global economy, a smaller board of directors would allow
more companies to incorporate and respond to the rapidly changing
economy. Likewise, there does not appear to be a rationale for
requiring that at least two of the board members be New York State
residents.  Many insurers in New York are now global enterprises and,
given the increased demands for improved corporate governance being
placed upon financial services corporations, it does not seem
necessary to require that two directors be state residents. The
primary consideration for selecting members of a company's Board of
Directors should be to identify individuals with superior intelligence
and high values who have an understanding of the business at hand,
regardless of their location.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2008: A.8767 S.2085-A
2009: A.1005-A

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act will take effect immediately.
